title: Avgolemono
subtitle: Greek egg and lemon soup
excerpt: Chicken stock with rice is finished with a tempered mixture of beaten eggs and lemon juice, creating a silky, creamy broth without any cream. Avgolemono means 'egg-lemon'. One of the simplest and most elegant soups in any cuisine. The tempering technique is the whole skill.
sourceNotes: Avgolemono means 'egg-lemon'. It is used both as a soup and as a sauce in Greek cooking. The technique of tempering eggs with hot broth creates a silky, creamy texture without any cream. One of the simplest and most elegant soups in any cuisine.

content.text: Avgolemono gets its silkiness from a careful tempering technique. Eggs and lemon are whisked together, then hot stock is added slowly, ladle by ladle, before the mixture goes back into the pot. If the eggs hit soup that is too hot too fast, they scramble. Work slowly and keep the heat very gentle at the end.
Bring chicken stock to the boil in a large saucepan. Add the rice. Reduce heat and simmer for 18-20 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Whisk eggs and lemon juice together in a bowl until frothy and well combined.
Ladle 3-4 spoonfuls of hot soup into the egg mixture, one ladle at a time, whisking constantly after each addition.
Pour the tempered egg mixture slowly back into the soup pot, stirring continuously.
Heat very gently for 2-3 minutes -- do not let it boil. Season. Serve immediately in warm bowls.

items.cause: Eggs not tempered or heat too high after adding
items.fix: Temper the eggs slowly with hot stock before adding back. Keep heat to a very gentle simmer only.

content.text: Greece and Cyprus. The national comfort food. Served when someone is unwell, at Easter, and as a starter at family tables. It is also used as a sauce poured over stuffed cabbage leaves or braised vegetables.
